climate.overview_html: The Super El Niño’s latest fingerprint on the US West Coast is a series of oceanic Kelvin waves now raising sea levels 15–30 cm along California, Oregon and Washington through February — amplifying erosion, flooding and king-tide risk for coastlines already strained by long-term sea-level rise and El Niño swell. Swiss glaciers lost 5.5% of their ice volume in 2026 (second-worst on record, GLAMOS) and the Copernicus Ocean State Report 10 documented the Mediterranean reaching its highest number of marine heatwave days in two decades — both stories from 30 September and still within the window. The EU’s Integrated Climate Resilience and Risk Management Framework is due for formal presentation on 20 October, embedding a 3°C global warming reference scenario as the mandatory planning baseline across EU institutions and Member States.

items.source: ABC News / phys.org / PBS NewsHour / Washington Times
items.headline: Super El Niño Kelvin Waves Now Raising US West Coast Sea Levels 15–30 cm; Erosion and Flooding Risk From California to Alaska Through February; Waves Moving North at 150 Miles Per Day
items.summary: A series of oceanic Kelvin waves tied to the 2026 Super El Niño began striking the US Pacific coast in early October, raising sea levels by 6 to 12 inches (15–30 cm) along the California shoreline and moving north at approximately 150 miles per day toward Oregon and Washington. NOAA says these waves are common during El Niño events but are amplified this year by the exceptional Super El Niño SST anomalies. The surge is expected to continue through February. Experts warn that the wave combines with two other hazards: above-average North Pacific swell associated with El Niño's altered jet stream, and larger-than-average spring tides from October to February — together creating compounded erosion and coastal flooding risk for shorelines already experiencing chronic retreat. The Kelvin wave is not a tsunami; it is a sustained thermal bulge up to 30 km wide that hugs the coastline, producing a persistent elevated sea surface rather than a breaking wave. The wave was expected to reach Alaska by mid-October.

items.headline: Swiss Glaciers Lose 5.5% of Ice Volume in 2026 — Second-Worst Annual Melt on Record; Aletsch Sets Record Since 1870; Alpine Melt Rate “More Than Twice as High” as Any Prior Five-Year Period; 20% Volume Lost Since 2021
items.summary: Swiss glaciers lost 5.5% of their total ice volume in 2026, the second-largest annual ice loss in the instrumental record after 5.9% in 2022. GLAMOS reported that the record-breaking European heatwave of summer 2026 combined with an unusually snow-poor winter to accelerate melting across the Alps. The Aletsch Glacier recorded its biggest annual melt since systematic monitoring began in 1870, losing 581 billion gallons of ice from July to September — four times Switzerland's annual water consumption. Over the past five years (2021–2026), Switzerland has lost nearly 20% of its total glacier ice volume — a rate 'more than twice as high as in any previously monitored five-year period.'

items.headline: Copernicus Ocean State Report 10 (OSR10): Mediterranean Hits Two-Decade High in Marine Heatwave Days; Arctic Ice Declining 490,000 km²/Decade; Black Sea and Mediterranean +4.6°C Peak Marine Heatwave Intensity; Ocean Heat Content Record in 2025
items.summary: The Copernicus Marine Service released its 10th Ocean State Report (OSR10) on September 30, 2026. Key findings: the Mediterranean Sea recorded its highest number of marine heatwave days in the 20-year record; the Black Sea and Mediterranean experienced peak marine heatwave intensity more than 4.6°C above normal in 2024; Arctic sea ice is declining at nearly 490,000 km² per decade; Mediterranean SSTs rose at 0.32°C per decade from 1982–2024; and global ocean heat content reached its highest level on record in 2025. The report documents accelerating threats to polar ecosystems, fisheries, and coastal communities from a rapidly warming ocean baseline.

items.headline: EU Integrated Climate Resilience and Risk Management Framework Due October 20: 3°C Reference Scenario; Duty on ‘Risk Owners’ Across Key Sectors; 100 Vulnerable Territories Identified
items.summary: The European Commission is due to present its Integrated Climate Resilience and Risk Management Framework on October 20, 2026 — a comprehensive legislative package embedding 'climate resilience by design' across EU policy. The framework establishes a 3°C global warming reference scenario as the mandatory baseline for climate risk assessment; a legal duty to assign 'risk owners' responsible for every major climate risk in key sectors (agriculture, transport, energy, finance, health); identification of 100 vulnerable European territories; and measures to mobilize private investment for resilience. The European Parliament Research Service described it as the most comprehensive EU climate adaptation legislative initiative since the 2013 EU Adaptation Strategy.

major_events.name: Super Typhoon Choi-Wan (JMA No. 27 / JTWC 27W) — SUPER TYPHOON; PASSING OGASAWARA; WEAKENING FROM PEAK
major_events.status: ACTIVE — As of October 5, Choi-Wan has reached Super Typhoon status with maximum sustained winds of 241 km/h (~130 kt, Category 4 equivalent) and central pressure of 916 hPa, a dramatic intensification from yesterday’s 950 hPa / Category 2-equivalent state; currently near 25.2°N, 146.5°E; October 5–6 is the closest-approach window for Chichi-jima and Haha-jima (Ogasawara Islands); peak was 250 km/h / 912 hPa; track recurving northeast toward extratropical transition east of Japan
major_events.impact: Typhoon-force conditions ongoing across Ogasawara Islands; all maritime access and inter-island flights suspended; ~3,200 permanent residents under evacuation guidance; 10–12 m seas near storm centre; JMA Typhoon Warning in effect; dangerous swells propagating across southern Philippine Sea

major_events.name: Hurricane Rachel — EASTERN PACIFIC; WEAKENING; NO LAND THREAT
major_events.status: ACTIVE — Rachel continues weakening in the Eastern Pacific south-southwest of Baja California; dry-air entrainment and wind shear accelerating weakening from Category 3; track westward and away from populated areas; 20th named storm of the 2026 Eastern Pacific season
major_events.impact: Dangerous 3–5 m swell along Baja California Pacific coast; no coastal warnings or watches in effect; storm tracking into open Central Pacific

weather.overview_html: Super Typhoon Choi-Wan intensified dramatically overnight to 241 km/h and 916 hPa — a full Super Typhoon upgrade from yesterday’s Category 2-equivalent state — now making its closest approach to Japan’s Ogasawara Islands on October 5–6 before expected extratropical transition northeast of Honshu. In the Atlantic, the NHC is monitoring a new Gulf of America disturbance with a 40% development chance; any organised system would drift toward the US Gulf Coast October 9–11 and would be named Isaias. Indonesia’s peat-fire haze crisis continues at ASEAN Alert Level 3, with 12 million people across Sumatra, Kalimantan and peninsular Southeast Asia under hazardous air quality driven by the Super El Niño’s sustained drought.

items.headline: Super Typhoon Choi-Wan: 241 km/h Sustained, 916 hPa — Rapid Intensification Overnight from Category 2 to Super Typhoon; Closest Approach Ogasawara October 5–6; Recurvature and Extratropical Transition Forecast Northeast of Japan
items.summary: Typhoon Choi-Wan underwent rapid intensification between October 4 and 5, deepening from 950 hPa / 45 m/s to a Super Typhoon with maximum sustained winds of 241 km/h (130 kt) and a central pressure of 916 hPa — its recorded peak before beginning gradual weakening. The storm is currently near 25.2°N, 146.5°E, making its closest approach to the Ogasawara Islands (Chichi-jima, Haha-jima) during October 5–6. JMA expects the storm to recurve northeast and undergo extratropical transition as it tracks toward the latitudes of the Japanese main islands. The storm's exceptionally large 1,300 km wind field means typhoon-force conditions affect Ogasawara even while the eye remains over open water. All maritime access to Ogasawara remains suspended; coastal evacuations are in effect for approximately 3,200 permanent residents.

items.source: NHC / Space Coast Daily / Spokesman-Review / BNO News
items.headline: NHC Tracking New Gulf of America Disturbance; 40% Development Chance Over 7 Days; Tropical Depression Possible Late This Week; Next Atlantic Name Is Isaias; Possible Gulf Coast Approach October 9–11
items.summary: The National Hurricane Center is monitoring a broad area of low pressure in the southwestern Gulf of America, assigning a 40% probability of tropical cyclone formation within seven days as of October 4, 2026. The 48-hour formation probability remains near zero. Environmental conditions are marginally conducive: SSTs are warm but wind shear is above ideal. Forecast models suggest any organised system would drift northward toward the US Gulf Coast between October 9–11. If it achieves tropical storm status, it would be named Isaias — the ninth named storm of the 2026 Atlantic season. The system represents the sole Atlantic activity in what has been a relatively quiet 2026 season.

items.headline: 2026 Southeast Asian Haze: Indonesia’s Worst Wildfire Season in 11 Years; ASEAN Alert Level 3 Active; 12 Million People Under Hazardous Air Quality; Super El Niño Drought Fuels Peat Fires
items.summary: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre's Alert Level 3 — the highest tier in its haze warning system — remains active as Indonesia's 2026 wildfire season, its worst in 11 years, sustains transboundary haze across Sumatra, Kalimantan and peninsular Southeast Asia. More than 12 million people face hazardous air quality. School closures continue in parts of Malaysia and Singapore; emergency room visits for respiratory complaints remain elevated. The Super El Niño is sustaining the crisis by delivering drought conditions to Sumatra and Kalimantan, providing optimal ignition and fire-spreading conditions for peatland burning. Legal analysts note that ASEAN's consensus-based sovereignty structure provides no mechanism to compel Indonesia to accelerate peat fire enforcement.

renewables.overview_html: Spain’s renewables reached 50.9% of the national power mix in September 2026 per grid operator REE (52.7% including self-consumption), a new monthly record underlining Europe’s clean-energy momentum. Adani Green expanded its Khavda BESS to 6.63 GWh — still the world’s largest single-location battery outside China — while Northland Power closed CAD$185 million for 300 MW / 1.2 GWh of capacity-market-contracted BESS in Poland. In the US, a McKinsey report finds tariff fragmentation, land constraints and a 4.5-year average interconnection queue have raised US solar LCOE 15–20% above 2023 levels, stalling an estimated 120 GW of pipeline.

items.headline: Spain Renewables Hit 50.9% of Power Mix in September 2026 — New Monthly Record; 52.7% Including Self-Consumption; Wind, Solar and Hydro Drive Record; 50 GW Solar Milestone Passed in February
items.summary: Spain's electricity grid operator Red Electrica de España (REE) confirmed that renewable sources accounted for 50.9% of national electricity generation in September 2026, rising to an estimated 52.7% when distributed self-consumption is included. The result sets a new monthly renewable share record for Spain, driven by strong wind output in northern regions and continued solar capacity additions since Spain crossed the 50 GW solar milestone in February 2026. The result underscores Spain's position as one of Europe's most rapidly decarbonising major power markets, alongside Germany which tracked 60.7% renewable share year-to-date through September 2026 per Fraunhofer ISE data.

items.source: Adani Green Energy / ESS News / PV Magazine India
items.headline: Adani Green Energy Khavda BESS Expands to 6.63 GWh — World’s Largest Single-Location Battery Outside China; Over 50% of India’s Operational BESS at One Site
items.summary: Adani Green Energy Ltd (AGEL) expanded its operational BESS capacity at Khavda, Gujarat from 3.55 GWh to 6.63 GWh on October 2, 2026, commissioning the new block in 10 months from construction start. Khavda now holds the world's largest operational single-location battery installation outside China. AGEL accounts for more than 50% of India's total operational BESS capacity of approximately 12.6 GWh. The milestone was reached 14 months after on-site BESS construction first began at the Khavda complex, which hosts one of the world's largest co-located renewable energy complexes, with solar, wind and now 6.63 GWh of dispatchable battery storage enabling grid-balancing and evening peak service for Gujarat and national grid operators.

items.headline: Northland Power Closes CAD$185 Million Financing for 300 MW / 1.2 GWh Poland BESS (Kamionka + Mieczysláwów); 17-Year Capacity Market Contracts; Green Loan Structure
items.summary: Northland Power closed approximately CAD$185 million in project financing on September 30, 2026 for two BESS projects in Poland: Kamionka (100 MW / 400 MWh) and Mieczysławów (200 MW / 800 MWh). Both projects carry 17-year capacity market contracts with the Polish electricity system operator and are structured as green loans supplemented by government grants from Poland's National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management. Commercial operation is targeted for 2028. The capacity market contracting structure providing long-term revenue certainty underpins project finance — a model being replicated across Central and Eastern European BESS deployment where wholesale price volatility limits merchant-only financing.

items.headline: U.S. Solar and Storage Face Structural Cost Headwinds: McKinsey Report; Tariff Fragmentation, Land Constraints and 4.5-Year Average Interconnection Queue Raise LCOE 15–20% From 2023; 120 GW Pipeline Stalled
items.summary: A McKinsey & Company report published October 2, 2026 finds that despite record-pace US solar and battery additions, three structural constraints are adding significant friction: trade-policy fragmentation driving equipment cost inflation; limited land availability in low-congestion grid zones near load centers; and grid interconnection delays averaging 4.5 years nationally. US solar LCOE is now 15–20% higher in nominal terms than 2023 levels, partially eroding gains from continued technology cost reductions. The authors project that addressing grid queue reform and tariff certainty would unlock an estimated 120 GW of stalled project pipeline by 2029, and recommend accelerated FERC Order 1920 implementation as the highest-priority policy lever.

items.headline: Renalfa IPP and Eurowind Inaugurate 242 MWp Solar + 773 MWh BESS Hybrid Park in Bulgaria; Among Europe’s Largest Operational Hybrid Renewable Parks
items.summary: Romanian IPP Renalfa and Danish developer Eurowind Energy inaugurated a hybrid renewable energy park in Bulgaria combining 242 MWp of solar PV with 773 MWh of battery energy storage — among the largest co-located solar-plus-storage facilities in operational service in Europe. The project is structured to optimise revenues across day-ahead energy markets and balancing services. Bulgaria has emerged as a significant European BESS market following grid interconnection upgrades and integration into the European balancing platform. The project joins a growing cohort of 200+ MWh co-located storage parks in Central and Eastern Europe, signalling regional maturation of hybrid renewable development beyond the UK, Germany and Iberia.

items.headline: Australia: Synergy Proposes A$2 Billion Solar and Battery Addition at Warradarge Wind Farm in Western Australia; Would Be Among Largest Hybrid Renewable Projects in Southern Hemisphere
items.summary: Western Australian state-owned utility Synergy has unveiled plans to develop a A$2 billion (approximately US$1.3 billion) co-located solar and battery storage project at the site of the recently expanded Warradarge Wind Farm in Western Australia's Mid West region — currently the largest wind farm in the state. The proposal would add large-scale solar PV generation and grid-scale battery storage to the existing wind resource, creating one of Australia's largest hybrid renewable energy projects. The development reflects growing momentum for hybrid renewable projects that leverage existing transmission connections and site permits, reduce per-MW infrastructure costs, and improve dispatchability by co-locating complementary generation profiles.

science.overview_html: The week’s sharpest new result comes from arXiv: Boscu et al. demonstrate that a probabilistic deep learning emulator can reproduce the stochastic dynamics of sudden stratospheric warmings (SSWs) with interpretable latent structure — correctly capturing regime statistics, rare transition rates and the committor function for vortex disruptions that drive European winter cold outbreaks, published simultaneously in JGR Machine Learning and Computation. Carrying from last week, a Nature Climate Change study documents up to 50 additional heat-stress days per year in the most-impacted regions, with tropical nights warming faster than the hottest days (0.32 vs. 0.27°C/decade) — a critical finding for human thermal recovery planning. The Met Office and Alan Turing Institute’s FastNet MLWP model was published in peer-reviewed form in AIES this year, achieving physically realistic forecasts by combining a modified spherical-harmonic loss function with GNN architecture to preserve sharp frontal structures and storm cores that ERA5-trained models typically blur.

items.headline: Global Heat Stress Intensification (Nature Climate Change, Vol. 16): Up to 50 Additional Heat Stress Days Per Year in Most-Impacted Regions; Hottest Nights Warming Faster Than Days (0.32 vs. 0.27°C/Decade); Compound Daytime–Nighttime Events Rising Sharply
items.meta: Multiple authors · Nature Climate Change Vol. 16, pp. 989–996 (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02670-5
items.summary: A Nature Climate Change study examining global heat stress from 1950 to the present analysed daytime extremes, nocturnal heat and compound daytime–nighttime heat events. Key findings: heat stress days increased by up to 50 per year in the most-impacted regions (parts of South Asia, sub-Saharan Africa and the Arabian Peninsula); tropical nights are warming faster than the hottest days, at 0.32°C per decade versus 0.27°C per decade — a pattern with serious implications for human thermal recovery during heatwaves; and compound daytime–nighttime events (which prevent nocturnal cooling recovery) increased sharply in frequency since the 2000s. The study documents pronounced spatial inequality: low- and middle-income countries face disproportionate exposure even as total global heat stress expands.

items.source: arXiv / JGR: Machine Learning and Computation
items.headline: AI Emulation of Stochastic Sudden Stratospheric Warmings with Interpretable Latent Structure (arXiv 2610.02069): ResNet CVAE Captures Regime Statistics, Rare Transition Rates and Committor Function of Polar Vortex Disruptions
items.meta: Boscu, Hernandez, Alvarez Ventura, Finkel, Chattopadhyay, Hassanzadeh, Abbot · arXiv:2610.02069 / JGR ML&C doi:10.1029/2026JH001387
items.summary: Boscu et al. develop a probabilistic deep learning emulator for the stochastic Holton-Mass model of stratospheric variability — a canonical model for sudden stratospheric warmings (SSWs), the extreme polar vortex disruptions that trigger severe cold outbreaks across Europe and North America. The emulator is a ResNet-inspired Conditional Variational Autoencoder with six-layer encoder/decoder and explicit current-state conditioning. Key results: the emulator accurately reproduces short-term dynamics, steady-state probability distributions, regime persistence statistics, rare transition rates, the transition committor function, and the transition expected lead time of the physical model. PCA of the 32-dimensional latent space reveals unsupervised separation into four physically interpretable clusters corresponding to strong-vs-weak vortex regimes and stable-vs-transition-prone configurations. The interpretable latent structure is a significant advance: it means the emulator does not just match statistics but learns physically meaningful representations of dynamical regimes, opening pathways for AI-based early warning of high-impact SSW events.

items.source: Met Office / Alan Turing Institute / AIES
items.headline: FastNet: Met Office and Alan Turing Institute ML Weather Model Achieves Physically Realistic Forecasts Surpassing Operational Global Model Skill; Spherical-Harmonic Loss Preserves Sharp Fronts and Storm Cores; Published in AIES Vol. 5 Issue 3
items.meta: Multiple authors (Met Office / Alan Turing Institute) · Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems Vol. 5, No. 3 (2026) · AIES-D-25-0090.1
items.summary: The Met Office and the Alan Turing Institute published FastNet, a Graph Neural Network-based MLWP model that achieves physically realistic forecast quality by addressing a key failing of ERA5-trained models: the tendency to blur sharp atmospheric structures. FastNet uses a modified spherical-harmonic loss function that preserves the correct distribution of energy across atmospheric scales, keeping cold fronts, storm cores and mesoscale features crisp rather than over-smoothed. When evaluated at 1.5° resolution on 2022 as a hold-out year, FastNet surpasses the skill of the current Met Office Global NWP system on multiple headline metrics, approaches the performance of leading 0.25° ERA5-trained models, and was validated against real events including a UK heatwave (predicted 84 hours ahead) and historical analogue storms. Although not yet operational, FastNet is a significant step toward physically trustworthy AI-based forecasting. The model weights and technical overview are publicly available (arXiv:2509.17658; HuggingFace MetOffice/FastNet-global).

items.title: Rainmaker Raises $100M Series B to Scale Drone-Based Cloud Seeding Across the American West; First Private Company to Physically Validate Cloud-Seeding Results; 145 Million Gallons of Verified Freshwater Produced
items.body_html: Rainmaker closed a $100 million Series B on September 21, 2026, led by NOA VC, Upfront Ventures, DCVC, Lowercarbon Capital and Dream Ventures. The El Segundo, California company flies weather-resistant drones into winter storm clouds and releases silver iodide, which provides nucleation sites for ice crystal growth that ultimately falls as rain or snow. Rainmaker became the first private company to physically validate cloud-seeding results, recording 82 unambiguous seeding signatures over four months for more than 145 million verified gallons of freshwater — close to the annual water use of 1,800 American households. The company is using the Series B to pursue a larger ambition: building scientific and technical infrastructure to understand, influence and eventually mitigate extreme weather beyond traditional cloud seeding. Total disclosed funding now stands at approximately $131.3 million ($6.3M seed, $25M Series A led by Lowercarbon in May 2025). The raise places Rainmaker at the intersection of weather modification, water infrastructure and climate resilience in a year when drought conditions driven by the Super El Niño are acute across the American West.

items.title: Inox Clean Energy Completes $627.5M Acquisition of Vena Energy India’s 6 GW Renewable Portfolio; Operating Capacity Expands to 4 GW; Total Pipeline Exceeds 12 GW; GIP (BlackRock) Exits India
items.body_html: Indian IPP Inox Clean Energy has completed the acquisition of Vena Energy India for INR 60 billion (US$627.5 million), finalising a deal originally announced in June 2026. The portfolio acquired from BlackRock-owned Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) comprises 1.2 GW of operational renewable assets, 1.8 GW at advanced development stage, and 3 GW of early-pipeline projects across solar, wind and hybrid. Following the transaction, Inox Clean Energy’s operating and near-operational portfolio expands to approximately 4 GW while its total development pipeline exceeds 12 GW, making it one of India’s largest independent renewable energy platforms. The deal marks GIP’s full exit from the Indian renewable energy market. The transaction is the largest inbound M&A deal in India’s renewable sector of 2026 and reflects ongoing consolidation as developers seek scale ahead of India’s 500 GW clean-energy target.
